turns.text: I've got a chest infection that's been going on for a week and I'd rather avoid antibiotics if I don't need them. How do I handle this well?
Why do most chest infections not need antibiotics? How does the body clear them?
What genuinely helps recovery — fluids, rest, steam, anything else?
If I saw a doctor, how would they decide whether it's bacterial and needs treatment?
What do respiratory doctors say are the signs that a chest infection has become something more serious?
A friend swears by honey and lemon and a humidifier at night. Is there anything in that?
Someone else said steam inhalation with a towel over your head. Helpful or old wives' tale?
I've had terrible reactions to antibiotics before and I can't afford a visit. How would I raise those reactions if I do end up seeing someone?
Which symptoms mean it needs antibiotics or urgent care regardless?
Could you give me a plan — what to do at home this week, what to monitor, and the point at which I go and get seen?
